title: Know the Design, Pick the Attack: Sentence-Keyed Watermarks for LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.34505v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A watermark lets the provider of a language model recognise the text its model wrote, which matters more as generated text becomes hard to tell from human writing: provenance underpins academic integrity, the fight against misinformation and new regulation. Providers have started to watermark the text of their models, and to explain how their watermarks work. Explaining a watermark, however, also tells an attacker how to break it, and there are two ways to do so: reword the text to erase the mark, or learn the mark and copy it onto text the model never wrote. Each attack has been studied on its own. We study an attacker that reads the published design to choose between them: it erases the watermarks that are hard to learn and forges the ones that survive rewording. translated_title: 了解设计，选择攻击：面向大语言模型的句子键控水印
translated_abstract: 水印让语言模型的提供者能够识别其模型生成的文本，随着生成文本越来越难以与人类写作区分，这一点变得愈发重要：来源追溯支撑着学术诚信、打击虚假信息以及新的法规监管。提供者已经开始为其模型的输出文本添加水印，并公开解释其水印的工作原理。然而，解释水印的工作方式同时也告诉了攻击者如何破解它，破解方式有两种：改写文本以抹除水印标记，或者学习该水印并将其复制到模型从未生成过的文本上。以往这两种攻击方式都是被单独研究的。我们研究了一种读取已公开的水印设计并在这两种攻击之间进行选择的攻击者：它会抹除难以学习（伪造）的水印，并伪造能够经受住改写攻击的水印。面对这种自适应攻击者，我们所比较的所有现有水印均告失败。为此，我们提出了KeyedLex，它从上一句的语法中读取其密钥，而改写对语法的改变很小。
tldr: 论文提出了一种自适应攻击者，通过阅读公开的水印设计在改写抹除和伪造复制两种攻击间择优选择，能击败所有现有水印，并据此提出KeyedLex水印——从上一句的语法中读取密钥，从而同时抵御两类攻击。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces an adaptive attacker that reads a watermark's published design to choose between paraphrase-based erasure and forgery attacks, defeating all existing watermarks, and proposes KeyedLex, which reads its secret key from the grammar of the previous sentence to resist both attacks.
